clue.text: Knowing about old pages becoming loose

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go round the next pieces

parts.note: fly is informal for knowing or sharp-witted

explanation.surface: A worn old book whose pages are coming away from the binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something limp and slack, not held firm, is loose in the sense of hanging freely.

clue.text: A legitimate target, Aunt Sally for example

definitions.meaning: someone who may rightly be criticised or attacked
Aunt Sally is a British fairground and pub throwing game, so literally a game at a fair

explanation.surface: An Aunt Sally is a person set up to be attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acceptable to attack, and literally describes a game played at a fair.

clue.text: Drama after away defeat?

indicators.note: after means the drama word follows the away word

parts.note: out means away, not at home
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: Theatrics following a loss on the road, an away defeat in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent by playing better is a synonym of defeat as a verb.

clue.text: Part flour, a little at a time

parts.note: a piece is a part
meal is coarsely ground grain, a kind of flour

explanation.surface: A baker adding part of the flour gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: Done gradually, bit by bit, is the meaning of this adverb.

clue.text: Part of speech given at one by male, word for word

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in which a man recites something exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating something exactly, using precisely the original wording, is the meaning of the Latin-derived adverb.

clue.text: Poker-faced, and lost for words?

definitions.meaning: showing no feeling on the face
playfully, without expressions, that is without phrases to say

explanation.surface: A card player who keeps a blank face and says nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means showing no emotion, and read literally means lacking phrases.

clue.text: Dealer, almost penniless

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a broker is a dealer in stocks or goods

explanation.surface: A trader who is nearly out of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no money at all is the informal sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Abridged film associated with a fairy queen

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the film title loses its last letter

parts.note: Titanic is the 1997 James Cameron film

explanation.surface: A shortened film about a queen of the fairies.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream she is wife of Oberon and ruler of the fairies.

clue.text: Complaint from team about leaders of Football League

indicators.note: about means the team name goes round the letters that follow

parts.note: Man U is short for Manchester United, the football team

indicators.note: leaders of means the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A grumble from a club concerning the bosses of the Football League.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild cold exaggerated by a man as severe illness is a humorous term for an ailment.

clue.text: Depressed over note, and nearly drunk, take a trip here?

indicators.note: over means placed above, in a down entry the first piece sits on top

parts.note: down means depressed
a memo is a note

indicators.note: drunk signals that the letters of nearly reel into a new order

explanation.surface: Feeling low after a message, and tipsy, someone takes a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for nostalgic recollection is a figurative journey into the past.

clue.text: Bad pint outside free house having a lot of problems

indicators.note: outside says the first jumbled set goes round the second
bad here signals that the letters of pint are spoilt into a new order
free signals the letters of house are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor pint served at a pub not tied to a brewery, a 'free house' in British terms.
explanation.walkthrough: A British free house is a pub not tied to one brewery; here 'free' is only a scrambling signal, and the pint's letters split to wrap the house's.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being in serious trouble, beset by difficulties, matches having many problems.

clue.text: Frequently fall in value after shares initially dropped

indicators.note: dropped means that letter is taken away

parts.note: prices soften when they weaken or decline

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of shares is used

explanation.surface: A market report: stock values regularly slip once shares fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are synonymous adverbs describing something happening many times.

clue.text: Sailing ship's gone out with maximum on board

indicators.note: on board means taken inside, carried within the other letters
out signals the letters of gone are put out of order

parts.note: all is the maximum, everything possible

explanation.surface: A sailing vessel departs with as many aboard as it can carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A large old Spanish multi-decked vessel is a type of sailing ship.

clue.text: 'Everlasting Love' finally learnt with different arrangement

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of Love is used
a different arrangement means the letters of learnt are reordered

explanation.surface: A musician has learnt the song 'Everlasting Love' in a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that lasts forever, without end; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Prime Minister, extremely believable? Perhaps

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister

indicators.note: extremely means the two end letters of believable

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Prime Minister is truly credible.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister from 2016 to 2019.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs expressing possibility rather than certainty; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Soft target not hard to come across, so it's said

indicators.note: so it's said signals a sound-alike: the spoken phrase is spelt differently

parts.note: not hard is easy, and to come across is to meet

explanation.surface: A vulnerable target that is simple to find.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a victim or opponent easily overcome or exploited.

clue.text: Book me in King's Head with a member, female

indicators.note: head means the first letter of King's

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Booking a room at a pub called the King's Head with a female MP.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Head is a common British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Hitler's autobiographical manifesto, a specific book.

clue.text: Cunning about soldiers discharged in a corrupt manner

indicators.note: about means the cunning word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: sly means cunning
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
did means discharged, carried out a duty

explanation.surface: Cunning dealings over soldiers being dismissed dishonestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in a base, dishonest or sleazy way is what this adverb describes.

clue.text: Rich source of oil, also containing diamonds

parts.note: oil is drawn from a well

indicators.note: containing means the word for also holds the next letter

parts.note: too means also
D is the abbreviation for diamonds, the card suit

explanation.surface: An oil well that also yields diamonds would make anyone wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective means prosperous or wealthy, a synonym.

clue.text: Feeling movement after onset of earthquake

indicators.note: after means the movement word comes after the first letter
onset of means the first letter of earthquake

parts.note: motion is movement

explanation.surface: Ground movement felt as a quake begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling such as joy or fear is a synonym of the noun.

clue.text: Keen on securing right opening

indicators.note: securing means holding the next letter inside

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Someone eager to land the correct first move.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction or opening passage, of a song or speech, is informally called by this short word.

clue.text: Acrobat one used to drink with?

explanation.surface: An acrobat who joins a drinking companion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a performer of somersaults and a straight-sided drinking glass.

clue.text: Jobless heading off, possibly for a Greek island

indicators.note: possibly signals the remaining letters may be rearranged
heading off means the first letter is removed

explanation.surface: An unemployed person heads off to a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an island in the north-east Aegean Sea, belonging to Greece.

clue.text: Thrifty management shown by small company spreading money about

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next piece
spreading signals the letters of money are spread into a new order

parts.note: CO is the short form of company

explanation.surface: A small firm manages its finances prudently by distributing cash carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges MONEY into E...NOMY, placed 'about' CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful, frugal handling of resources is what this word means as a noun.

clue.text: Love unaltered watering hole

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
as is means unaltered, in its current state

explanation.surface: A beloved bar left just as it was.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile desert spot with water where animals and travellers drink is literally a watering hole.

clue.text: Similar to barking wildly

parts.note: like means similar to
barking is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: Like a dog barking wildly.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means intensely or furiously, synonymous with wildly as an adverb.

clue.text: Some Chablis, seventh heaven

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A glass of Chablis, the French white wine, puts the drinker in seventh heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven used loosely means perfect happiness or delight, a synonym.

clue.text: Gathered adult son looked like failing to get on

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

indicators.note: failing to get means the following letters are left out

parts.note: to resemble is to look like
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A grown-up son who looked like he would never get on in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought or come together in one place, as a crowd or parts are collected, is a synonym.

clue.text: Ominous, nun ringing home

indicators.note: ringing means encircling the next piece

parts.note: a nun is called a sister
in means at home

explanation.surface: A nun telephoning home with a foreboding message.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something threatening, suggesting harm to come; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Public brawl — see Father after a fine a year later

indicators.note: after means the father piece follows the a-fine pair
later puts the a-year pair after the rest

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A priest witnesses a street fight a year after a fine was paid.
explanation.definitionFit: In law this word names a fight in a public place that disturbs the peace.
